Marissa / Rachel — attaching the peering diagram. Key points for Medilink security review:
1) Egress paths: Privatelink endpoints terminate in EU-only subnets. Outbound telemetry (health metrics) is routed to our EU telemetry cluster; agent-level telemetry that contains operational metadata is scrubbed of tenant identifiers unless flagged by a customer for debug.
2) Keystore custody: Customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) are supported — we can show a diagram with the KMS partitioning. For Redwood-managed keystores, operator access is split by operator group id; the manifest shows grouping (no single operator has global keystore modify rights).
3) Operator access controls: We enforce JIT (just-in-time) SSH with auditable justification and a short-lived cert model for operator sessions. All operator actions are logged to immutable storage with retention metadata included in the SOC2 excerpt.
4) Network proof: We can provide a sanitized traceroute and peering AS path for a demo tenant to show no egress to non-EU ASNs. We will need Medilink's tester IP to run the trace.

If Medilink needs the BGP/route table exports for compliance evidence, we'll prepare those under an access-controlled share (link above).

Ben Carter
VP, Infrastructure
ben_carter@redwood.com

--- end forwarded message ---

Let me know the IP/range you want us to use for the network trace. I can produce the sanitized traceroute (no operator identities) by EOD.
